styles.name: Explainer Short
styles.tagline: Voice-led explainer, every word on its beat
styles.pitch: A voice-over explainer for any product: a light brand stage, kinetic type that lands on every spoken word, props and real product moments, a CTA tail.
needs: What it is about (a topic, raw notes or a script)

laws.title: The voice drives everything
laws.text: Every visual event lands on a spoken word; the word appears on the frame the voice says it.

laws.title: Hook in under two seconds
laws.text: A bold uppercase claim in the top third, first 2 s.

laws.title: The screen carries the key words
laws.text: Not every spoken word goes on screen: the hook word, the proof word, the climax line.

laws.title: One type style, one accent
laws.text: One font per video, one accent colour from the brand, and one serif-italic accent word at most.

laws.title: Never change the background
laws.text: The brand stage stays: light paper, soft glows, a fading dot grid, grain.

laws.title: No overlapping text, no dead air
laws.text: Something new every 0.5–1 s; never a 1.5 s stretch without a new element.

laws.title: Hook → proof → climax → CTA
laws.text: The owner's raw text is input, not copy: one idea per line, verified facts only, a new angle every video.

styles.skill:
**Direction (owner 2026-10-09)**
- Script: the owner's raw text is input, not copy. Rewrite it into hook → proof → climax → CTA, cut duplicates, one
  idea per line, verified facts only. Keep the owner's beats (e.g. "comment captions and I'll send you the link").
- Every new video takes a NEW angle and hook form.
  Log the angle in the video's script.txt header so the next one can avoid it.
- Not every spoken word goes on screen. The screen carries the key words (hook word, proof word, climax line);
  the visuals carry the rest. Typing notes go on the words that are SHOWN, on our voice's frame.
- Text entry: centred lines → each word RISES from below inside its own box (masked, small overshoot);
  left-aligned lines → each word comes in from the RIGHT with an elastic, damped overshoot (not a plain slide);
  one hero word per scene may SLAM (scale-in). Renderer: `motion` on a line (rise | elastic | slam | slide).
- Font: the owner will name the brand font from a screenshot; until then Inter + one serif-italic gradient accent
  (the site's "just upload." look). Font is ONE variable per video (`FONT` in build.py).
- Product shots are the real product: live captures in a drawn browser window; the camera dives to the detail
  (GitHub repo name + highlighter sweep); a search bar types the brand and GROWS into the site; a big cursor clicks
  through the real flow (upload → captions written → Looks → Export) with titles on chips above the moving UI;
  the payoff is a real output clip. Captures via Playwright (`playwright-core`, channel chrome) are fine, no need to ask.
- Competitor logos are allowed when the owner asks: their own app icons (site icons / Wikimedia),
  struck through one per spoken word, drained of colour, dropped out of frame (`kill` on an image).

- Voice is first person: "We just killed…", not "Someone". Re-voice only the changed line and splice it in (keeps the take).
- More easing: rise 16 f (outBack), elastic settles ~0.6 s (exp −5.5, cos 12.5), slam 9 f, image enters SPRING.soft,
  scene enters arrive +24 f, exits 10 f.
- Background (owner 2026-10-10, DEFAULT now): no chip clutter. TWO relatable brand assets (logo mark / product icon) drift
  slowly in opposite corners (top-left, bottom-right, partly off-frame), alternating grey ↔ full colour every ~6 s; an asset
  pulses to full colour when the voice mentions it (`backdrop.corners`, `pulse`). Glows + faint grid + a few sparkles stay.
  Owner 2026-10-10 v2: corners BIG (~280–300 px) and fully inside the frame with their own reserved space (no text in the
  top-left 20–330 × 60–370 or bottom-right 760–1060 × 1560–1860 zones; s1qa checks it), animated: spring in, dip-and-pop on
  every scene cut, lift on mention, scale out at the end.
  Owner 2026-10-10 v3 (FINAL rule, overrides v1/v2 motion): corner assets sit HALF off the frame edge (left edge top, right
  edge bottom, ~360–380 px), rotate in at the start, rotate out at the end, and stay completely STILL in between
  (`still: true`: no drift, no grey cycle, no beat dips, no pulses).
- NO overlapping text, ever (owner 2026-10-10): s1qa now flags any touch (text↔text >2%, text within 8 px of a card/icon/phone,
  24 px of a corner logo). Slam words grow away from the previous word (left-anchored, ≤1.22×). QA can't see collisions inside one
  line: always check the slam frames on the still sheet.
- Background must never feel empty: on top of the glows + grid, out-of-focus caption chips (WOW, viral, NO WAY…) float
  in the corners with deep parallax and twinkling four-point sparkles drift (`backdrop.chips`, `backdrop.sparkles`).
  Keep chips off the text: check the still sheet for collisions.

## 1. Format
- 9:16, 1080×1920, 30 fps (refs) [confirmed]. 60–110 s [confirmed].
- Voiceover drives everything: every visual event lands on a spoken word [observed].
- One continuous canvas: 1–14 hard cuts per video; scenes change by elements entering and leaving [confirmed].
- Something new enters every 0.5–1 s; no dead air [observed].

## 3. Typography
- Font: **Roboto** (single-storey g, Roboto Y/t) [confirmed in frames]; bundled in the engine as `roboto` (OFL).
  A brand file may override it.
- Word-by-word reveal locked to the VO [confirmed, frame by frame at 30 fps]: the new word arrives light grey
  (~#555 → black), slides a few px left into its slot with a decelerating ease, and darkens fully in **6–8 frames**.
  No vertical slide. The centred line re-balances as words are added; the whole block keeps a slow drift.
- Mixed hierarchy in one sentence: small regular words + bold/italic/UPPERCASE key words at 1.5–2× size [observed].
- Lists: `+` sparkle bullets, one item per spoken phrase [observed].
- Hook: bold uppercase stacked claim, top third, first 2 s [observed].

## 6. Structure
1. 0–2 s hook: uppercase claim + cutout face + accent burst.
2. Story / proof: screenshots, numbers, lists.
3. Value list ("you get… + item").
4. CTA tail (pattern; wording from the brand file): comment-keyword → lead magnet mock-up → "follow <brand>" → logo.

## 7. Things that are felt but easy to miss (check every video)
VO-locked timing · grey→black word fill · mixed-size hierarchy per sentence · overshoot pop + idle drift ·
paper shadows on off-white + dot grid · single accent colour · no dead air · near-zero hard cuts ·
quiet, dense SFX (felt, not heard) · identical CTA tail.

styles.name: Hinglish Promo
styles.tagline: Fast kinetic type, every word on screen
styles.pitch: A fast Hinglish promo on cream paper: every spoken word on screen, stacked small / HUGE / small, comic marks, whips and zoom-throughs, a follow-and-comment CTA.
needs: The comment keyword for the CTA

laws.title: Every spoken word on screen
laws.text: About 2.8 words a second; a new shot every 1.2–2 s.

laws.title: Small / HUGE / small
laws.text: Anton caps stacked by weight of meaning, one Instrument Serif breather line.

laws.title: Never the same transition twice in a row
laws.text: Rotate whips, zoom-throughs and recedes, each with real motion blur.

laws.title: Never flat
laws.text: Letters scatter in, key words slam; marks, cards and the cursor keep every frame alive.

laws.title: Five beats
laws.text: Call-out hook → pain → "bas iss website pe aao" + 3 steps → 3 proof lines → CTA (follow + comment KEYWORD).

styles.skill:
## 0. Owner rules (inherited from Style 1 §0, apply here too)
- Never self-grade; the owner's eye + side-by-side with a ref decides.
- Everything in the video is ours: drawn in code, the product's own site assets/captures, generated props, our voice.
- Every video uses NEW props (product website assets allowed). SFX from the owner's kit (`styles/style-1/sfx/`, map.json).
- Risers: max 2 per video, complete, ending on the hit. Typing note on every spoken word.
- Owner 2026-10-09: Claude's Hinglish reads broken. Claude drafts the beats + facts; the owner rewrites the Hinglish and
  sends the voice MP3. Build on-screen words from the owner's final text, never from Claude's draft.

## 1. Format and pace
- 1920×1080, 30 fps (refs). 18–30 s. ~2.8 words/s. A new shot every 1.2–2 s; never a still camera.
- Every spoken word appears on screen when it's said (the video demos captions).
- Story (5 beats): call-out hook → pain (time / rival tool) → "bas iss website pe aao" + 3 steps → 3 proof lines + "aur haan,
  Hinglish bhi" → CTA: follow + "comment KEYWORD" + "link main bhej dunga". The comment CTA drives engagement.

## 2. Stage and type
- Cream paper (brand stage colour) + soft diagonal window-blind shadows drifting + light vignette. Never flat.
- Anton (ALL CAPS) for everything; one serif italic line (Instrument Serif) per video as a breather.
- Stacked hierarchy per shot: small line (90–130 px) · HUGE word (220–440 px) · small line. Size solved to fit 1720 px.
- One accent family from the brand file. Marks: comic burst, marker
  strike, hand-drawn circle, highlighter wipe, underline swoosh, tick badge, four-point sparkles.

## 3. Motion (renderer: `packages/library/src/components/style2-timeline.ts`)
- `scatter` (default): letters drop in from lower right, tilted, 0.9 frame apart, back-out ease over 8 frames, smeared by velocity.
- `slam`: from 1.9× scale, 3–4 frames, blurred while fast. `rise`: letters spring up. `type`: one letter per 1.2 frames.
- Scene `in`: `whip-l/r/u/d` (both shots smeared along the travel), `zoom` (zoom-through, radial blur), `recede`, `cut`.
  Rotate them; never the same twice in a row. Scenes start 4 frames before their first word.
- Cards: `fly` (rise + tilt), `pop`, `zoom`, `drop`, `left/right`; idle float; `blur` = depth of field; look clips loop
  inside `loop: [0.3, 1.75]` (they are blank at both ends). Drawn cards: `timeline`, `upload`, `credit`, `code`, `caption`.
- Cursor keys `[frame, x, y, click]`, comment box (types the keyword, send click), pill (FOLLOW → pressed), profile card.

## 4. Sound
- Voice −18 LUFS, music **5 LU under** (refs 4.7), SFX stem from events (whoosh per whip, pop per card, click per cursor
  click, typing per word, snap per slam word, riser into the reveal + one into the CTA). Master −14 LUFS, ≤ −1 dBTP.
- Bed: upbeat ~110–120 BPM from the library (`funky-chunk` 115 BPM from 12.54 s) until the owner gives one; CC-BY credit in credits.txt.

styles.name: Launch Film
styles.pitch: A 20–45 s cinematic launch film about the one feeling the product gives: lit 3D worlds, a camera that never stops, type as design, every cut carried by light or motion.
styles.engine: Blender sets + Remotion (React Three Fiber), built per film

laws.title: One feeling
laws.text: The film is about one feeling the product gives (relief, pride, speed, calm, power). Every beat serves it; a beat that only informs is cut. The feeling is named in brief.json before any picture exists.

laws.title: Every frame is a poster
laws.text: Pause anywhere: a clear hero (30-60 % of the frame), three depth planes, a lit world, nothing cropped by accident, nothing empty. If a frame would not work as the thumbnail, it is not finished.

laws.title: Light is the subject
laws.text: One motivated key (window, practical, screen, sun), one coloured rim, one practical in frame, haze or dust so the light has a body. Shadows are coloured, never grey. No scene is lit by "ambient".

laws.title: Rich, never busy
laws.text: A hero world has >= 30 dressed objects, one hero, the rest supporting in soft focus. A bare primitive on a void is the single most common failure of this style.

laws.title: Real scale, real materials
laws.text: Metres, bevels, thickness. One material accent per film (glass, chrome, balloon, velvet, paper, neon), everything else matte toy plastic with coloured bounce; reflections come from an env map.

laws.title: Colour is a script
laws.text: A palette strategy (decks), 3-4 colour states across the film, colourfulness in the register's band (pastel >= 45, candy >= 50, dark by design with ONE saturated accent). Beige and grey voids are banned.

laws.title: The camera is a character
laws.text: Always moving through depth; one dialect per film; speed ramps are the signature (slow floor, 10-25x spikes with a 2-6 frame tail, on words / beats / cuts). Still cameras and 2D zooms are not Style 3.

laws.title: Type is design
laws.text: One pairing per film from the type deck, one accent treatment, words as objects in depth when they are heroes, sizes measured against the frame, never default bold sans, never cropped by accident.

laws.title: The cut is a move
laws.text: Every cut has a carrier (bloom, object at the lens, occluder, whip, word); outgoing ramps up, incoming starts at speed; white (or the world's dark) is the house colour of a cut; no crossfades.

laws.title: Sound is half
laws.text: The bed is chosen FIRST and the film cuts on its grid; SFX felt, not heard; a riser ends on the hit; music + SFX by default, VO only when human (the owner's) or explicitly wanted.

laws.title: Finish everything
laws.text: Grade (curves), grain, vignette, leaks/halftone per register, CA fringe, bloom on light sources, sheen sweeps, dust, overshoots, contact shadows, idle life on everything that hangs. A draft look is a failed film; the micro-detail pass (style-3-finish) is not optional.

laws.title: Never the first idea
laws.text: Three concepts from three different hands, a critic, a pick, then "can it be better?" once more. The same question at every stage (picture, prop, move, type, sound) and again on the 1 fps sheet.

8. **Type is design.** One pairing per film from the type deck, one accent treatment, words as objects in depth when

9. **The cut is a move.** Every cut has a carrier (bloom, object at the lens, occluder, whip, word); outgoing ramps

10. **Sound is half.** The bed is chosen FIRST and the film cuts on its grid; SFX felt, not heard; a riser ends on the

11. **Finish everything.** Grade (curves), grain, vignette, leaks/halftone per register, CA fringe, bloom on light

    once more. The same question at every stage (picture, prop, move, type, sound) and again on the 1 fps sheet.

## 3. Uniqueness (same URL + same prompt = a different film every run)
- `s3_deal.py deal videos/<slug> --n 3` deals three hands (shape, world, hero, engine, camera, palette, light, type,
  transition, thread, material, music) from `styles/style-3/library/decks.json` with a clock seed, avoiding every row of
  `videos/FILMS.md` in >= 4 of 6 fingerprint columns. The hand is a constraint: the concept must live at its
  intersection. A card may be redealt ONCE per concept with a logged reason (it breaks the brief, not "I prefer").
- The kept hand goes into `brief.json.hand`; `s3_deal.py check` before Gate 1; `s3_deal.py log` after Gate 3.
- Metaphor bank, pictures and set layouts of refs and logged films are never reused for the same beat.

## 4. Owner rules (standing; every correction is added here the same day)
- **2D / 3D rule (same day):** 3D only where it earns it: 3-4 signature moments (the product as an object, one
  transformation, the reveal), <= 40 % of runtime, each at product-photo quality (or a Blender plate, or cut). The rest
  is the REAL product big on clean fields and confident type: the 2D craft of Style 1/2, elevated. A film that is 100 %
  real-time 3D exposes every weakness for 25 s.
- **Gate 1 is never skipped**, even when told "go" or "fastest": the owner sees the storyboard, then 4 real frames, before
  any build. "Go" means start, not skip. Deliver the storyboard as a document first when asked.
- The decks' quirky cards (rooftop, arcade, kitchen, paper, pet, hand, bot, plane) are a "character" tier: off unless the
  brief asks for playful. Default tier for launches: studio-void, product-space, creator-room, night-city, gallery.
- Never self-grade: the owner's eye + a side-by-side decides. Bring the sheet and the critic's verdict, not a score.
- Everything shipped is ours: Blender/R3F builds, CC0 assets (logged), the product's own site captures, our music
  (CC0/CC-BY with credit), our SFX (`styles/style-1/sfx/`). Reference clones are private studies, never posted.
- Premium footage first (`styles/assets/README.md`); real product media only, nothing faked on a screen.
- Repo is public: never commit refs, renders, music or third-party meshes. Commit only when asked.
- Gate 1 shows REAL look frames (engine renders), never SVG storyboards or word tables alone.

styles.name: Metaphor Essay
styles.tagline: One sentence, one picture, voice typeset
styles.pitch: A 30–60 s voice-led thought piece: every sentence becomes one cut-out picture made of its nouns, floating in a single-hue spotlight world, every word typeset as it is said.
styles.engine: Remotion S4Film (data-driven) + cut-out pictures + your voice
needs: The thesis: what the essay argues

laws.title: One world
laws.text: One hue in four stops (pale floor -> mid -> top -> saturated corners) with the ink in the SAME hue (`cards.ts WORLD`). It never changes inside a film or a series. Unity comes from the TREATMENT: every picture, whatever its source, is mapped into the hue, stands on the floor with a soft shadow, gets the same grain.

laws.title: One sentence, one picture, made of that sentence's nouns
laws.text: Literal, fusion (two nouns in one object), scale shift, replacement, collection (`style-4-write` §4). If a line cannot be pictured, the LINE is rewritten.

laws.title: The picture lands with the cut; the voice is typeset over it
laws.text: Every spoken word on screen, letter by letter from its spoken onset (0-4 frames late, done before the word ends). Never an empty field after a cut.

laws.title: Hierarchy is meaning
laws.text: KEY words heavy condensed caps; connectors light italic, tucked into the key words' gaps (left stacks, tails, small rows); ONE coined CONCEPT in heavy italic. A lockup is a block 45-65 % of frame width, above and/or below the picture, never over it.

laws.title: Photographic truth
laws.text: Pictures are real things with real material and texture (archival photos, product shots, textured renders); smooth clay/plastic renders go flat and toy-like in the hue (dry run 2026-10-12). Natural colour only where the colour IS the meaning, at most 2 pictures per film. Real people, logos and products are extracted, never generated.

laws.title: The antagonist has a language
laws.text: The thing the essay argues against gets ONE visual dialect (halftone, scanline, melt, bleed... from the deck), used every 3-4 pictures and only on the lines where it acts.

laws.title: An essay about the viewer's own world
laws.text: A thesis someone could disagree with; specific names, years, numbers (all sourced in brief.facts); a coined term (for a brand: often the brand's own word); a turn; a last line that could be quoted alone. For a brand film every line is about the brand's customer and the brand's craft (owner rule §4): no abstract lectures, no hype words, no price-list of services.

laws.title: Grounded, lit, alive
laws.text: Every picture stands on the floor with a cast + contact shadow in the ink hue that STAYS on the floor when it lifts; it is lit from the world's top-left key (relight, rim, a sliding glint); it lands with a blur-in push / turn-in / fly / drop and never stops after landing (heroes are lit reliefs that really turn, plus bob, rock, tilt); it exits by accelerating into the cut. Hard cuts (the world stays, so a cut is a page turn); print grain + halftone; the voice leads, a bed 7-8 LU under it, and the full Style 1 SFX kit under every event (owner rule §4).

laws.title: Something new every second
laws.text: Letters typing, a print landing, a device drawing, a scan passing; a new picture every 2-5 s (refs: mean 3.5 s). Quality never drops: the last third is checked as hard as the first.

laws.title: Never the first idea, never self-graded
laws.text: Three hands, three writers, a critic, a pick, one more "better?" pass; the owner's eye and a side-by-side with a reference (for feel, never to copy) decide, not a score. **The transfer test** (how every rule above was chosen, and how new ones are added): would it survive a different topic, world, font and author? If yes it is grammar and belongs here. If no, it is the reference's content and goes in the breakdown's "never copy" list and the decks as a `ref` card.

styles.name: Premium Reel Edit
styles.tagline: Your footage, edited like a pro reel
styles.pitch: Your talking-head, avatar or podcast clip becomes a premium 9:16 reel: word-synced captions on the chest, punch-ins every phrase, a full-screen scene every few seconds, every cut hidden in light.
styles.engine: Remotion (edit1) per reel, from your footage

laws.title: Every reel is bespoke
laws.text: A direction first: concept, type, palette, b-roll, scenes, music. Never a recolour of an earlier edit.

laws.title: Captions on the chest
laws.text: At 62–70 % of the frame height, 1–3 words at a time, every word on the frame it is spoken.

laws.title: Never a static face
laws.text: A slow push on every shot and a +5–8 % punch-in every phrase or two.

laws.title: A full-screen scene every ~4 s

styles.skill:
## 0. Owner rules
- The only thing that matters is the quality of the final video. Claude has full creative liberty on the edit.
- **Every reel is bespoke** (owner 2026-10-11). Before building, write `videos/<slug>/DIRECTION.md`: the reel's concept
  and mood, its own type system (font pairing from scratch for this reel/brand), palette, b-roll plan (what visual
  carries each line), scene designs, effect + transition palette, music mood. Then build new scene components for it.
  Allowed to reuse: engine plumbing (EDL, word timing, footage framing, caption timing/letter-build mechanics, mixer,
  tools). Not allowed: the previous reel's look — its fonts, palette, scene designs (eye room, funnel, arc carousel,
  ruler…), signature effects or end card. Test: put a still of the new reel next to the last one; if it reads as the
  same edit recoloured, redesign.
- **B-roll** is part of the job: the brand's own site/product media and captures, owner-supplied clips, footage from
  the reel itself (re-framed, speed-ramped, split), and motion graphics drawn in code. Stock or generated media from
  outside sources: ask the owner before downloading.
- Never self-grade: one still sheet per pass, then the MP4; the owner's eye decides. Fix what the sheet shows first.
- Everything new in the edit is ours: drawn in code, the brand's own assets (site logos, client logos already saved
  from the brand's site), system emoji, our music (MotionEasy CC-BY library) + the owner SFX kit (`styles/style-1/sfx/`).
- Honesty: no invented numbers, stats or customers. Client logos only if the brand's site shows them (brand file `facts`).
- Inherited sound rules (style-1 §0): risers complete and ending on the hit, at most 2; never the same accent twice in a row.
- Owner corrections 2026-10-10:
  - Use the ORIGINAL voiceover: the source's own audio track cut by the EDL (`e1_voice.py --src full`), not a demucs
    stem (only separate when the source has a loud bed).
  - Theme is white + orange only: no black/dark scenes. The spotlight room is cream with an orange beam and
    brown/orange icons; the "problem" beat is a warm desaturate (sepia), not black-and-white.
  - Natural grade: no saturation push (contrast 1.03, sat 1.0, warm overlay ≤ 5 %), light washes at ~0.55.
  - No fake ad-manager tags/chips (Interests, Age, Location…) on the opening card; emojis are fine.
  - Music: cinematic + upbeat. Default to the owner bed `styles/style-1/music/bed.mp3` (136 BPM, builds to a drop at
    14.0 s and a climax at 25.5 s), looped on bar lines so the drop and climax land on key beats, ~9 LU under the voice.

## 1. The craft in one page (measured on the reference; the grammar, not the look)
1. **Captions** sit at ~62–70 % of frame height on the chest, 1–3 words at a time, every word on the frame it is spoken.
   Registers: `sm` white sans 46 px · `sc` signature script 118 px (overlaps the big word's top) · `big` heavy grotesk
   ~150 px, tracking −5.5 %, cream→peach gradient, letter-by-letter build over the spoken word · `mid` bold white→warm
   grey ~104 px for short punches. Later words keep their final slot (no re-centring). Phrases swap by blur-dissolve.
   One gag per video at most: a letter becomes an object (reference: OO → eyeballs) or a reticle locks onto the word.
2. **Never a static face**: slow push on every shot + a jump-cut punch-in (+5–8 % snap, exp settle) every phrase or
   two. Punch-ins double as crops: frame the face in the upper third and keep the source's baked graphics out.
3. **A full-screen scene every ~4 s** replaces the face for one idea: dark blueprint room with a white eye/light
   (algorithm, attention), handwriting on peach (a statement), a build (funnel, steps), cards on an arc (a list),
   logo/years ruler (proof). Pick the scene from what the line MEANS, not what it says.
4. **Every cut hides in light or motion**: coloured light wash (2–4 f rise, ~25 f fall), a light ring orbiting the
   subject before it, strip-split wipe (8 f), zoom-blur push, white flash into a mood shift (mono for the problem beat).
   The source's own cuts get hidden the same way (detect them: ffmpeg `select='gt(scene,0.2)'`).
5. **Motifs carry across cuts**: the bouncing ball becomes the light in the dark room; the CTA pill opens the end card.
6. Grade warm (contrast 1.07, sat 1.12, soft-light peach), dark lower gradient for type, grain 6 %.
7. Sound: voice −14 LUFS master, music ~11 LU under the voice, SFX ~20 dB under (felt, not heard), ~4 cues/s.

s3.about: the story's shape: how the 20-45 s argument is built (register-independent)

cards.name: The contrast
cards.line: 'The hardest part isn't X. It's Y.' The viewer's own belief, corrected in two beats.
cards.use: Beat 2 must be ONE word on its own card. The product is the answer to Y, never to X.

cards.name: The overheard line
cards.line: Opens on someone else's words (a DM, a comment, a text, a review) that create the demand.
cards.use: Real-looking UI, 3D, at the lens. The product answers the line by the reveal.

cards.name: The thesis
cards.line: A bold claim as the first frame ('Not everything has a tutorial'), then the film proves it.
cards.use: The claim must be a true, slightly uncomfortable sentence; the proof is pictures, not more claims.

cards.name: The object's journey
cards.line: One physical object (the product's icon made real, a file, a frame of footage) travels from problem to payoff through every world.
cards.use: The object is the carrier at every cut; it changes state (dull -> lit, flat -> 3D, grey -> colour).

cards.name: Before / after, one take
cards.line: The same scene twice: the camera moves THROUGH the before and arrives in the after without a cut.
cards.use: Change only what the product changes (captions, colour, light); keep everything else identical so the eye measures the difference.

cards.name: The countdown
cards.line: Three (or five) numbered things, each a world of its own, landing on a drop.
cards.use: Numbers as big 3D objects that the camera passes; the last number is the product.

cards.name: The machine
cards.line: Input goes in one side, the product is the mechanism in the middle, the output comes out transformed.
cards.use: Build a real mechanism (press, conveyor, kiln, printing press, vending): the camera follows the thing THROUGH it.

cards.name: A day in the life
cards.line: Morning to night for one creator; the product appears when the day gets hard.
cards.use: Light is the clock (dawn -> noon -> golden hour -> night); each time of day is a colour state.

cards.name: The question
cards.line: 'What if...?' asked once, then answered by showing, never by saying.
cards.use: The question card is white and quiet; the answer bursts in colour. Use at most once per brand (ref A).

cards.name: The unmask
cards.line: Something ordinary peels, cracks or opens to reveal that the product was inside all along.
cards.use: The reveal mechanism is physical (shell, wrapper, paint, watermark) and ends at the lens.

cards.name: The recipe
cards.line: Three ingredients fall in, the result rises out: the product as a kitchen, a lab, a darkroom.
cards.use: Each ingredient is one proof (a real feature); the result is the real output, big.

cards.name: The wants montage
cards.line: Rapid cuts of what the viewer wants (the dream), then the one thing in the way, then the product removes it.
cards.use: Music-led (register B); the wants are beautiful, the obstacle is ONE object, the removal is a single satisfying move.

cards.name: The reverse reveal
cards.line: Open on the finished, viral result; rewind to show it was made with the product in minutes.
cards.use: Rewind as a visible world effect (time runs backward, objects un-break) then a hard cut to real time.

cards.name: The confession
cards.line: First person, honest: 'I paid for this for two years.' Then the turn.
cards.use: Only with a human VO or on-screen type in first person; quiet type, intimate world (a desk at night).

s3.about: the family of places the film lives in (one hero world + the product space + type cards; or many small worlds)

cards.name: Creator's room
cards.line: A desk, a monitor, a ring light, shelves, plants, posters, cables: the place the viewer wants to work in.
cards.use: >= 30 dressed props, one window light + one practical (LED strip, screen glow). Three angles minimum.

cards.name: Night-city penthouse
cards.line: Floor-to-ceiling glass, a city of lights below, one desk lamp, rain or haze.
cards.use: Bokeh city as the far plane; screens as the key light; reflections on the glass.

cards.name: Studio void with practicals
cards.line: An infinite cyc in one colour, lit by visible practical lights (tubes, bulbs, a soft box).
cards.use: The practicals ARE the design: coloured tubes, a ring light, a hanging bulb; floor reflections; haze.

cards.name: Paper world
cards.line: Everything is card stock: pop-ups, cut-outs, folds, tabs; a lamp on a tabletop.
cards.use: Real paper thickness and fold shadows; one colour printed per layer; macro lens with bokeh.

cards.name: Miniature city
cards.line: A tilt-shift town on a table: tiny streets, cars, billboards that carry the type.
cards.use: Billboards and shop signs are the type cards; a drone-like camera; tilt-shift blur top and bottom.

cards.name: Workshop / garage
cards.line: Pegboard tools, a workbench, sawdust in the light, a project under a lamp.
cards.use: Warm tungsten + one cold window; dust in the beam; the product is the tool that fits the hand.

cards.name: Library / archive
cards.line: Stacks, ladders, drawers, index cards, brass lamps; knowledge as a place.
cards.use: Deep perspective rows for travel shots; the type as index cards and spines; green lamps.

cards.name: Greenhouse / garden
cards.line: Glass panes, leaves in backlight, pots, a watering can, a gardener's table.
cards.use: Sun through leaves = moving gobo; growth as the metaphor; green + one warm accent.

cards.name: Rooftop at dusk
cards.line: String lights, a chair, the skyline, a laptop on a crate; the sky is the colour script.
cards.use: The sky gradient changes per beat (dusk -> night); string lights as bokeh; wind in cloth.

cards.name: Train / metro at night
cards.line: A window seat, lights streaking past, a phone in hand, reflections.
cards.use: Hyperlapse streaks outside = free motion; the phone screen is the product; reflections double the frame.

cards.name: Arcade / neon alley
cards.line: Cabinets, neon signs, wet floor reflections, steam; the product on a cabinet screen.
cards.use: Neon as the type; the drop as a cabinet lighting up; magenta + cyan with black.

cards.name: Museum gallery
cards.line: White walls, spotlights, plinths; the product's output hung as art.
cards.use: Each proof is a framed piece under its own spotlight; the camera walks the room; silence then the drop.

cards.name: Underwater / aquarium
cards.line: Caustics on everything, bubbles, a slow float; the product is the one dry, lit object.
cards.use: Caustic light as a moving texture; slow-mo world; blue-green + one warm light.

cards.name: Cloud sky
cards.line: Objects floating in a bright blue sky with cumulus; balloons, umbrellas, kites.
cards.use: Lightness and relief beats; type behind objects in depth; strong sun glare.

cards.name: Abstract product space
cards.line: UI panels, cards, glass and gradients floating in a colour field (the demo world of any register).
cards.use: Three depth planes (card in front, panel, far field); liquid glass; measured gradients.

cards.name: Kitchen at golden hour
cards.line: Tiles, copper pans, a window over the sink, steam; the product plated like food.
cards.use: Backlit steam, a cutting board macro, bowls as containers for the proofs.

s3.about: what the product IS on screen (the thing the viewer must see big and often)

cards.name: The real UI through glass
cards.line: Live captures of the product inside a liquid-glass card or a monitor, the cursor doing the real flow.
cards.use: Big: >= 45 % of frame height; frosted panel + rim + sheen; the result appears where the cursor presses.

cards.name: The output as an object
cards.line: The product's result (a caption, a render, a page) lifted off the screen as a physical, lit, bevelled thing.
cards.use: Extrude it, give it material (chrome, candy, glass), let the camera orbit it.

cards.name: The device
cards.line: A phone or laptop playing the real output, close, as the light source of the shot.
cards.use: Screen brighter than 1.0 (bloom), content fills the frame at least once; the device has a stand, a cable, a case.

cards.name: The print
cards.line: The output printed: posters, cards, a photo strip, billboards; a shop window.
cards.use: Paper has edges, shadows, a slight curl; prints are pinned, taped, framed.

cards.name: Light itself
cards.line: The product is a light source: a beam, a lamp switching on, neon lighting up; the output appears where the light falls.
cards.use: Haze so the beam is visible; the switch-on is the reveal; everything the light touches gains colour.

cards.name: The crowd of outputs
cards.line: Dozens of real outputs as a wall, a fan, a river, a ring: abundance.
cards.use: Instanced, varied, all real; the camera travels along it; one comes forward as the hero.

s3.about: the metaphor engine: how a feeling becomes a physical event

cards.name: Scale
cards.line: Too many / too big / too small: a row that never ends, a giant word, a tiny creator under a huge watermark.
cards.use: Repetition + desaturation = fatigue; one huge object at the lens = pressure.

cards.name: Gravity
cards.line: Things fall, float, drop into containers, hang in bullet time.
cards.use: Weight is emotion: the pain is heavy (drops, thuds), the product is light (floats, rises).

cards.name: Transformation
cards.line: A becomes B in one continuous move: flat becomes 3D, grey becomes colour, paper becomes glass.
cards.use: The transformation IS the reveal; it must be visible mid-way (no cut in the middle).

cards.name: Journey
cards.line: From here to there: a corridor, a road, a cable, a river of cards the camera follows.
cards.use: Travel shots with high parallax; the destination is the product.

cards.name: Mechanism
cards.line: Press, crank, pull, conveyor, gear: a visible cause and its effect.
cards.use: The user's action is the cause (a click, a tab pulled); the output is the effect, within 4 frames.

cards.name: Weather and light
cards.line: Dark to light, rain to sun, fog clearing, a sunrise through a window.
cards.use: The colour script is the weather; the product is the sun.

cards.name: Assembly
cards.line: Parts fly together into a whole: letters into a word, shards into a logo, pieces into a device.
cards.use: Spring settles with overshoot; the last piece lands on the beat.

cards.name: Peel / unmask
cards.line: Wrappers off, paint scraped, a watermark torn away, a page turned.
cards.use: The peel reveals the real output underneath; the torn piece flies at the lens.

cards.name: Mirror / reflection
cards.line: The before and the after as a reflection, a split, a window between two rooms.
cards.use: One camera move crosses the mirror line; reflections must be real (planar reflection or a mirrored set).

cards.name: Growth
cards.line: Seeds to plants, a sketch to a building, a dot to a city: things grow on the beat.
cards.use: Growth curves eased (never linear); the fully grown thing is the product's output.

s3.about: the camera dialect for the whole film (one per film; variety comes from the beats, not from mixing dialects)

cards.name: Elegant push and arc
cards.line: Slow pushes, arcs of 30-60 deg, rush-ins into screens; roll up to 40 deg over a long arc (ref A).
cards.use: One spike per ~1.5 s on an accent; letterbox the opening; symmetric wides for 'normal life'.

cards.name: Tumble and chase
cards.line: Tumbles between worlds, chases along ribbons, objects AT the lens, roll +-45 deg, 2-frame smears (ref B).
cards.use: Cut on the beat grid; 40 % of ramps on cuts; top-down and steep dutch angles.

cards.name: Slow drift, low angle
cards.line: Drifts and slow pushes, low angles up at big shapes, the world in slow motion (ref C).
cards.use: 9x ramps with 6-frame tails; heavy vignette; particles; the camera never hurries.

cards.name: The one take
cards.line: A single continuous camera move through every world, hidden cuts inside occluders and whips.
cards.use: Plan the path first; every world connects physically (a door, a window, a screen); 3-4 hidden cuts max.

cards.name: Top-down tabletop
cards.line: Looking down at a desk from above, tilting to 3/4 for action, macro for detail.
cards.use: Hands-free: objects slide, pop and spin; a tilt-down is a cut; paper and tools at real scale.

cards.name: Macro first
cards.line: Extreme close-ups (85-135 mm): a marker tip, a key, a bevel, then pull out to the world.
cards.use: Shallow DOF, breathing handheld; textures must be real (grain, fibre, brushed metal).

cards.name: Orbit-centric
cards.line: Everything revolves around one hero object; the camera orbits, the world turns around it.
cards.use: Bullet time once; the hero changes state on each quarter turn.

cards.name: Drone
cards.line: High, fast, banking passes over a landscape or a city; dives to a detail.
cards.use: Banking roll keyed to turns; a dive is the rush-in; hyperlapse <= 2.5 s.

s3.about: the palette STRATEGY (the brand's colours fill it in; the strategy decides dominance, contrast and the arc)

cards.name: Pastel gradients
cards.line: Soft saturated gradients (peach, pink, lavender) with white; darks read as plum, never black.
cards.use: Colourfulness >= 45; every 2D card a measured mesh gradient; coloured shadows.

cards.name: Dark + one neon
cards.line: Near-black teal or navy with ONE neon accent (magenta, cyan, amber) and bone white type.
cards.use: Vignette 0.5+, grain 0.06, haze; the accent is a light source in frame.

cards.name: Monochrome + accent
cards.line: One hue in many values (all blues, all creams) and a single contrasting accent on the hero.
cards.use: The accent appears only on the product / the accent word; everything else stays in the family.

cards.name: Complementary split
cards.line: Two opposite families (teal / orange, violet / gold) split by beat: pain in one, product in the other.
cards.use: The cut from pain to product is a colour cut; keep both families saturated.

cards.name: Warm-to-cool arc
cards.line: The film travels from one temperature to the other (cold office -> warm studio, or dusk -> night).
cards.use: The arc is the story; measure it in 3-4 colour states; the brand colour is the destination.

cards.name: Candy
cards.line: Saturated glossy colours (magenta, cherry, lilac, mint) on white, clearcoat materials, balloon type.
cards.use: Reflections via an environment map; white backgrounds, coloured contact shadows; high energy.

cards.name: Paper, ink and one colour
cards.line: Cream stock, ink line work, one printed colour that floods in at the turn.
cards.use: The flood is the reveal (the colour arrives with the product); paper texture visible.

cards.name: Sunset
cards.line: Golden hour: amber key, violet shadows, a pink sky; long shadows and haze.
cards.use: Backlight + glare in frame; the sky is a gradient that moves over the film.

s3.about: the light rig of the hero world (one motivated key, one practical, one rim)

cards.name: Window sun + gobo
cards.line: Low warm sun through a window and blinds: bands of light across walls and desk.
cards.use: Gobo behind the camera; a second soft sun for broad shadows; dust in the bands.

cards.name: Blown-out window
cards.line: A window so bright it hazes the room; white bloom at the edges; soft everything.
cards.use: Bloom 0.4+, haze; silhouettes against the window; the product the only sharp thing.

cards.name: Neon practicals at night
cards.line: Tubes and signs light the set; wet or glossy floors reflect them.
cards.use: Each tube a real light + an emissive mesh; rim from the opposite colour.

cards.name: Soft top studio
cards.line: A large soft source above, gentle falloff, coloured bounce from the floor.
cards.use: Product-space default; add a coloured rim so forms separate from the backdrop.

cards.name: Single spotlight in darkness
cards.line: One hard cone, everything else falls to black; the spot moves or widens on the reveal.
cards.use: Visible cone in haze; the spot's edge is the composition; type inside the pool of light.

cards.name: Golden backlight
cards.line: A low sun behind the subject: rim everywhere, glare in frame, long shadows toward the lens.
cards.use: Lens flare restrained (one glare source), haze for shafts; fill from the sky colour.

cards.name: Screen glow only
cards.line: The device lights the room: cool key from the screen, the rest warm and dim.
cards.use: The screen content changes the room's colour (a proof per colour); intimate framing.

cards.name: Bulb string / lanterns
cards.line: Many small warm points: string lights, lanterns, a marquee; bokeh discs everywhere.
cards.use: Each bulb an emissive sphere + a small point light near the hero; the drop lights them all.

s3.about: the typographic pairing for the whole film (fonts in packages/engine/assets/fonts; one pairing per film)

cards.name: Geometric sans + italic serif accent
cards.line: Plus Jakarta Sans 700 for lines, Instrument Serif italic for the one accent word.
cards.use: Accent word 1.1-1.3x, glow on pastel; sentence case.

cards.name: Condensed grotesk + script
cards.line: Archivo / Inter Tight 800 caps for slams, Pacifico for a single warm word.
cards.use: Giant cropped words on the beat; the script word small and off-grid.

cards.name: Serif display + small caps
cards.line: Fraunces 300-600 (and italic) for heroes, Inter small caps with wide tracking for lines.
cards.use: Two sizes in one line (3:1); words blur in one by one; bone white or gold.

cards.name: Mono + display
cards.line: JetBrains Mono for labels, timestamps and UI; Bricolage Grotesque 800 for headlines.
cards.use: Labels in corners like a HUD; headlines centred; one colour for mono, ink for display.

cards.name: Rounded sans + outline
cards.line: Plus Jakarta 800 solid for the hero word, the same face outlined (1.5 px) for the rest.
cards.use: Outline type sits in depth behind objects; solid type in front.

cards.name: Extruded 3D type + flat small caps
cards.line: Our own font as 3D geometry (s3_typeface.py) for 1-2 hero words, Inter small caps as 2D lines.
cards.use: 3D words get material and light (ink face, gold sides); framed for every frame of their shot.

cards.name: Editorial serif + hairline sans
cards.line: Fraunces 500 for the sentence, Inter 300 for a tiny kicker above it.
cards.use: Magazine spreads: left-aligned, generous margins, a hairline rule.

cards.name: Poster condensed
cards.line: Anton for one giant word per card, Inter 500 for the small line under it.
cards.use: The giant word crops the frame on purpose; the small line never does.

s3.about: the film's SIGNATURE transition (used 2-3 times; every other cut uses a plain carrier)

cards.name: Bloom match-cut
cards.line: A screen or light blooms white; the next shot opens from the same white with the carried word in place.

cards.name: Tumble
cards.line: The camera rolls and accelerates; two smeared frames hide the cut; the next world is still rolling.

cards.name: Speed-line burst
cards.line: Props fly at the lens with radial speed lines; one white frame; an ink stroke wipes to the next shot.

cards.name: Star iris
cards.line: A four-point sparkle grows exponentially through the lens to white.

cards.name: Occluder wipe
cards.line: The camera passes behind a dark foreground object (a column, a chair back, a hand); the cut lives inside it.

cards.name: Page peel
cards.line: The frame is paper; a corner curls over the lens and reveals the next shot.

cards.name: Strobe card
cards.line: The frame tilts as a 3D card, every third frame black, a hue flicker, lands on the big word.

cards.name: Colour glitch
cards.line: Four frames of inverted hue + RGB split + streak bars.

cards.name: Frame to card
cards.line: The whole frame shrinks into a rounded card on black, flickers, the next title appears.

cards.name: Light through a pillar
cards.line: Passing a bright gap between two dark shapes, a flash wipes the cut.

cards.name: Zoom-through
cards.line: Rush into a screen, a window or a word until it fills the frame; the inside is the next world.

cards.name: Shutter / blinds
cards.line: Horizontal slats (blinds, louvres, a shutter) close over the frame and open on the next.

cards.name: Liquid wipe
cards.line: A colour pours, splashes or fills the frame (ink in water, paint, a wave) and drains into the next shot.

s3.about: the recurring character or thread that links the film

cards.name: The 3D cursor
cards.line: A real extruded arrow that flies, lands, presses and rides things (refs A, B).

cards.name: The paper plane
cards.line: A folded paper plane that carries the message between worlds.

cards.name: The light beam
cards.line: A projector, torch or sun beam that reveals what it touches.

cards.name: The product icon, physical
cards.line: The brand mark as a bevelled object with weight that appears in every world.

cards.name: The camera bot
cards.line: A tiny drone or camera-on-legs that films the film (seen in reflections, at the edges).

cards.name: A hand
cards.line: A stylised 3D hand (gloved, toy-like) that pulls, presses and holds.

cards.name: None: the music
cards.line: No character; the beat and the light carry the film (ref C).

cards.name: A pet
cards.line: A toy-like cat or bird that watches, knocks things over, lands on the reveal.

s3.about: the one material accent of the film (everything else matte toy plastic)

cards.name: Liquid glass
cards.line: Frosted panels with rim lensing, sheen sweeps, coloured shadows.

cards.name: Chrome
cards.line: Mirror metal on the hero object or the hero word; reflections of the set.

cards.name: Balloon gloss
cards.line: Inflated, clearcoat, candy-coloured letters and props.

cards.name: Velvet / satin
cards.line: Deep soft fabric with sheen falloff; curtains, ribbons, cloth that flows.

cards.name: Card stock
cards.line: Paper with thickness, fold shadows, printed texture.

cards.name: Neon tube
cards.line: Glass tubes with a bright core and a coloured halo; flicker on switch-on.

cards.name: Glazed ceramic
cards.line: Smooth glazed surfaces with a soft specular; mugs, tiles, figurines.

cards.name: Soft-touch plastic + brushed metal
cards.line: Matte rubbery bodies with brushed-metal rings and buttons (premium hardware).

cards.name: Wood and brass
cards.line: Oak grain and warm brass details; lamps, frames, handles.

s3.about: the music direction (the bed is chosen FIRST from packages/library/src/music.gen.ts moods; the film cuts on its grid)

cards.name: Soft
cards.line: Gentle, warm, 80-100 BPM; VO or type-led films; lifts on the reveal.

cards.name: Uplifting
cards.line: Bright, hopeful, 100-120 BPM; the standard launch feel.

cards.name: Groove

s4.about: how the 30-60 s argument is built

cards.name: Two lives, one act
cards.line: The same act done by two people for opposite reasons (one for survival, one for status); the difference is the thesis.
cards.use: Alternate their pictures 2-3 times, same framing, so the cut itself argues. The thesis is said once, over the second life.

cards.name: Anecdote -> today -> named idea
cards.line: A dated story (person, year, a concrete object), the same act today, the gap named as a coined term.
cards.use: The anecdote must have ONE physical detail that becomes a picture (sheet metal, a violin). The coined term lands at ~45-55 %.

cards.name: The prediction
cards.line: A specific claim about the next 5 years, then the evidence that is already visible today.
cards.use: Open on the future picture, then go back to three present-day proofs, then return to the future picture changed.

cards.name: The myth, corrected
cards.line: A belief the viewer holds, shown as true, then turned over with one fact.
cards.use: Give the myth its best picture first; the correction must be a picture too (never only a number).

cards.name: The hidden cost
cards.line: Something we gained, then the invoice nobody showed us, line by line.
cards.use: Each cost is one picture of the SAME object getting worse (the thread degrades). End on what to keep.

cards.name: The quiet instruction
cards.line: A practice explained as if to a friend: what to do, why it works, what it protects.
cards.use: Three steps max, each a physical act with the hands. The why is an analogy from the lens card.

cards.name: The letter
cards.line: Written to someone (your past self, a student, the reader in 2035).
cards.use: Second person all the way; one object the letter keeps returning to (the thread).

cards.name: The question chain
cards.line: Each line answers the previous one with a sharper question; the last answer is the thesis.
cards.use: At most 4 questions; each answered by a picture before the voice answers.

cards.name: The biography of an object
cards.line: One ordinary object's life (made, used, replaced, missed) carries the whole argument.
cards.use: The object is the thread; every picture is it in a new situation (scale, fusion, collection).

s4.about: the first sentence (the hook). 4-12 words, said in the first 2.5 s, with its picture on frame 1

cards.name: In <year>, <someone>...
cards.line: A year + a named person + a verb, in the first four words.
cards.use: The person's archival photo (public domain) on frame 1, the year as the first key word.

cards.name: Right now,...
cards.line: A live phenomenon with a number ('Right now, thousands of people...').
cards.use: The number must be true and sourced; the picture is the act, not the crowd.

cards.name: The impossible fact
cards.line: A true sentence that sounds false.
cards.use: Say it flat; the picture is the strangest literal version of it.

cards.name: The accusation
cards.line: 'You haven't... in a year.' The viewer as the subject.
cards.use: Gentle, specific, never shaming; the picture is the abandoned object (the unused thing).

cards.name: This is a...
cards.line: Name the object on screen as if handing it over ('This is a 400-year-old lens.').
cards.use: The object fills 50 % of the frame on frame 1; the next line says why it matters.

cards.name: The confession
cards.line: 'I stopped... and something strange happened.'
cards.use: First person, one specific detail, the picture is the stopped thing.

cards.name: The number that hurts
cards.line: One sourced number as the first key word.
cards.use: The number IS the picture's scale (a pile, a stack, a crowd of the same object).

s4.about: the field the essay borrows its analogy and its coined term from (the 'creative inflation' move)

cards.name: Ecology
cards.line: Monoculture, topsoil, invasive species, rewilding, succession.
cards.use: A landscape picture that changes state across the film (the thread).

cards.name: Medicine
cards.line: Immunity, dosage, placebo, side effects, withdrawal.
cards.use: The pill / the dose / the scan as fusion pictures.

cards.name: Physics
cards.line: Friction, entropy, inertia, resonance, pressure.
cards.use: A simple apparatus picture (a pendulum, a spring) that behaves like the idea.

cards.name: Architecture
cards.line: Load-bearing walls, foundations, scaffolding, ruins, renovation.
cards.use: The building's structure is the argument's structure; scale shifts (tiny people, giant beams).

cards.name: The kitchen
cards.line: Slow-cooked vs microwaved, fermentation, seasoning, reduction.
cards.use: Ingredients and tools as fusion objects; time is the hidden ingredient.

cards.name: The farm
cards.line: Seasons, soil, harvest, fallow fields, grafting.
cards.use: Hands and seeds; the seasons give the film a colour arc inside one hue.

cards.name: Navigation
cards.line: Maps vs territory, dead reckoning, the north star, GPS.
cards.use: Instruments as the thread (compass, sextant, map pins).

cards.name: Music
cards.line: Practice, tempo, silence between notes, tuning, improvisation.
cards.use: Instruments as fusion objects; the edit breathes on the bed's bars.

cards.name: Craft
cards.line: Apprenticeship, the patina of tools, kintsugi, the grain of wood.
cards.use: Hands working a material in close-up cut-outs.

cards.name: Sport
cards.line: Training camps, the last 5 %, the bench, the marathon wall.
cards.use: One athlete figure as the thread across situations.

cards.name: Slate / graphite

cards.name: Plum / aubergine

s4.about: the recurring object: it reappears in new situations (fusion, scale, collection) and carries a series across episodes

cards.name: Hands
cards.line: Archival hands doing things: holding, building, letting go.
cards.use: Scale shifts (a giant hand holding a tiny world) and the final picture.

cards.name: The hourglass
cards.line: Time as an object: filling, cracking, sand as the antagonist's material.
cards.use: Fusions (hourglass + city, hourglass + phone).

cards.name: The seed
cards.line: From seed to tree across the film.
cards.use: The thread grows as the argument grows.

cards.name: The ladder
cards.line: Climbing, rungs missing, a ladder to nowhere.
cards.use: Scale shifts; tiny figures on a giant ladder.

cards.name: The candle
cards.line: Attention as a flame: lit, guttering, relit.
cards.use: The flame is the one warm accent inside the hue.

cards.name: The compass
cards.line: Direction: spinning, broken, true.
cards.use: Lens: navigation.

cards.name: The paper boat
cards.line: Fragile effort carried by something bigger.
cards.use: Collections (a fleet), scale (one boat on a giant ocean).

cards.name: The matchstick
cards.line: One spark, burnt matches as proof of attempts.
cards.use: Collections of burnt matches as 'the climb'.

cards.name: The lighthouse
cards.line: A fixed point that guides; the beam device belongs to it.
cards.use: Signature device: beam.

cards.name: Thread and needle
cards.line: Repair, connection, slow stitching.
cards.use: The line device becomes a literal thread between pictures.

cards.name: The eye
cards.line: Attention, seeing, being watched.
cards.use: Archival engraving eyes, lenses, peepholes.

cards.name: The key / keyhole
cards.line: Access, locked potential.
cards.use: Fusions with the topic's objects.

s4.about: the visual language of the thing the essay argues against (engine fx); used every 3-4 pictures, only where the antagonist acts

cards.name: Halftone dots
cards.line: fx scan shape=dot: the object becomes print dots (mass production, sameness).
cards.use: Copies, imitation, media.

cards.name: Scanlines
cards.line: fx scan shape=line: the object is read by a machine line by line.
cards.use: Surveillance, measurement, metrics.

cards.name: Melt
cards.line: fx warp: the object loses its shape (heat, speed, overload).
cards.use: Burnout, haste, overconsumption.

cards.name: Ink bleed
cards.line: fx bleed: the object appears or dissolves as a spreading stain.
cards.use: Memory, spread, contamination, influence.

cards.name: Binary pour
cards.line: device binary: digits pour out of the object.
cards.use: Only when the antagonist IS software; never as a default.

s4.about: the film's signature attention device (others allowed once each)

cards.name: Hand-drawn arrow
cards.line: Dashed curve from a word to the picture: the essay pointing.
cards.use: When the line names a part of the picture.

cards.name: Drawn circle
cards.line: A hand circle around the detail that matters.
cards.use: Collections: circle the one that's different.

cards.name: Light beam
cards.line: A shaft of light finds the picture.
cards.use: Revelation, attention, the one that matters.

cards.name: Taped prints
cards.line: Pictures as taped photo prints on the field.
cards.use: Archival evidence, collections, memory.

s4.about: the last line (not in the fingerprint; vary it anyway)

cards.name: The aphorism
cards.line: One sentence that could be quoted alone.
cards.use: Its key word is the thread's name or the coined term.

cards.name: Next episode
cards.line: 'In the next episode,...' + one specific promise.
cards.use: The last picture opens the next episode (the chain).

cards.name: The question back
cards.line: A question to the viewer, answerable in a comment.
cards.use: Not 'what do you think?': a specific choice.

cards.name: The callback
cards.line: The first picture returns, changed.
cards.use: Same framing as frame 1, a new state.
